Instead, one will find stools where the clergy sit during services, a large blackboard at the head of the church, and an organ, typically very large. This design is common to all Presbyterian churches, as Presbyterianism was largely born out of Episcopalism. From the 8th to the 10th century, three dynasties contested for control of northern India: the Gurjara Pratiharas, the Gupta Empire, and the Chola Empire. The Gurjara Pratiharas were a powerful and wealthy army while the Gupta Empire was the wealthiest empire in the ancient Indian subcontinent. The Cholas governed northern India until the British colonized it in the late 1600s. The city of Bengal, then known as Calcutta, was part of the Pratiharas, but was annexed by the Gupta Empire after they gained control of northern India.
